title: Iterative Approximate Byzantine Consensus under a Generalized Fault Model
evidence_note: For the paper's synchronous directed-graph model, every reduced graph for every feasible fault set having exactly one source component is necessary and sufficient for IABC existence; algorithm trims extrema based on locally known feasible neighbor fault sets. Theory only; no deployment or asynchronous evidence.

title: Multiple Frequency Selection in DVFS-Enabled Processors to Minimize Energy Consumption
review_status: full-text section audit complete; sampled v2 independently rechecked
evidence_note: Rechecked against the fixed-frame v2 full text after discovering the earlier ledger incorrectly said v1. Simulation on fitted legacy-processor power models: MFS-DVFS gives 14.40% savings on random graphs and 27.0% on LU versus continuous-frequency optimum 14.84% and 27.81%; Gauss-Jordan only 0.11% vs 0.14%, attributed to absence of idle slack. These are simulations with fitted Transmeta Crusoe/Intel Xscale power curves, not measurements on physical processors.

title: An Analysis of Multi-hop Iterative Approximate Byzantine Consensus with Local Communication
review_status: full-text section audit complete; citation follow-up
evidence_note: Signed multi-hop relaying changes the communication model and can work over local/sparser links at the cost of flooding. Simulation is one Erdos-Renyi setting (30 honest, 14 Byzantine); no multi-seed uncertainty or communication-cost baseline reported.
